segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [soft wind rustling forest leaves] [softly] Close your eyes if comfortable and imagine every sound as a small transmitter hidden in a night forest.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Hear the whole forest at once. Let sound arrive before the mind decides what made it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Choose the most distant signal. Rest attention there as though a tiny lamp is blinking beyond the trees.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now find a middle-distance sound... something neither far away nor inside your body.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [soft fabric rustling] Tune to the nearest sound: breath, fabric, swallowing, or a quiet movement beside you.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Move from far... to middle... to near... allowing attention to travel without rushing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice a sound beginning, changing, and ending. No transmission remains exactly itself.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [thoughtfully] Release the categories and hear one living field. The forest needs no conductor.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Include the body that is listening and the silence that appears between signals.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes. Let the forest become an ordinary room again, still full of small transmissions.
